죄송합니다.forms: polite: 죄송해요 · past: 죄송했습니다 (no casual form)
죄송합니다.x: I'm so sorry to have kept you waiting so long.
죄송합니다.e: Literally 'guilty and fearful' + 합니다 — more formal than 미안합니다.
죄송합니다.t: More humble than 미안합니다. Use it with teachers, bosses, elders and customers.

코트.x: It was cold, so I wore a thick coat.
코트.e: From English 'coat'. 코트 can also mean a sports court, like 테니스 코트.

가다.x: I'm going to the sea with a friend this weekend.
가다.t: Destination takes 에: 학교에 가요. 안녕히 가세요 = goodbye (to someone leaving).

들어가다.m: to go in, to enter; to go back (home)
들어가다.x: It's cold, so let's go inside.
들어가다.e: 들다 (enter) + 가다 (go). Opposite: 나가다; 들어오다 = come in.
들어가다.t: 들어가세요 is also a polite goodbye: 'Get home safely.'

이사하다.x: I'm moving to a new apartment next month.
이사하다.e: Both parts mean 'move' — moving house. 이사 가다 = to move away.

먼저.forms: 먼저 + verb: 먼저 가세요, 먼저 드세요
먼저.t: 먼저 드세요 = 'Please eat first / go ahead.' A polite phrase you'll hear often.

빨리.forms: 빨리 + verb: 빨리 와요 · 빨리빨리 (hurry, hurry)
빨리.t: 빨리빨리 ('quick quick') is a famous phrase describing Korea's fast-paced culture.

그럼.forms: short for 그러면 · reply: 그럼요! (of course!)
그럼.m: then, in that case; of course
그럼.x: It's raining? Then I'll stay home.
그럼.e: Short for 그러면 (if so). 그럼요! = Of course!
그럼.t: 그럼 안녕히 계세요 = 'Well then, goodbye.' A natural way to end a conversation.

지나가다.m: to pass by, to go past; (of time) to go by
지나가다.x: The bus just went right past the stop.

나빠지다.m: to get worse, to go bad
나빠지다.x: As the weather got colder, my cold got worse.
나빠지다.t: -아/어지다 turns adjectives into 'become' verbs: 나빠지다, 좋아지다, 추워지다.

신기하다.x: Korea's subway system is really fascinating.
신기하다.t: Use 신기하다 for cool, surprising things, like 'Whoa, neat!', not for 'weird' in a bad sense.

월세.x: The monthly rent for this studio is 500,000 won.
월세.t: Korea also has 전세: you pay one large deposit, get it back later, and pay no monthly rent.

밤새.x: I couldn't sleep a wink all last night.
밤새.t: For 'to pull an all-nighter', say 밤을 새우다 (casually 밤새다): 어제 밤을 새웠어요.

이하.m: or less, under, below; the following
이하.ex: 키가 120센티미터 이하인 아이는 탈 수 없어요.
이하.x: Children 120 centimeters tall or shorter can't ride.

밀다.forms: 밀어요 · 밀었어요 · 밀 거예요 · 미세요 (ㄹ drops)
밀다.x: Even if I push the door hard, it won't open.
밀다.t: Door signs read 미세요 (push) and 당기세요 (pull).

훨씬.x: To Seoul, the train is much faster than the bus.

지원하다.x: I wrote my résumé to apply to that company.
지원하다.e: Literally 'will and wish'. A different 지원하다 (different hanja) means 'to support'.
지원하다.t: Use place + 에 지원하다: 회사에 지원하다 'apply to a company'.

보험.ex: 보험이 있어서 병원비가 많이 나오지 않았어요.
보험.x: I had insurance, so the hospital bill wasn't very high.
보험.t: To get insurance, say 보험에 들다 or 보험에 가입하다.

물가.ex: 요즘 물가가 너무 올라서 장보기가 무서워요.
물가.x: Prices have gone up so much lately that grocery shopping is scary.
물가.t: Pronounced [물까]; said [물가] without the tense sound, it means 'waterside.'

오염되다.m: to be polluted, to be contaminated
오염되다.ex: 공장에서 나온 물 때문에 바다가 오염됐어요.
오염되다.x: The sea was polluted by water from the factory.
오염되다.t: For 'X pollutes Y,' use 오염시키다: 공장이 강을 오염시켰어요.

어휘.ex: 한국 드라마를 보면 어휘를 늘릴 수 있어요.
어휘.x: Watching Korean dramas can help you build your vocabulary.
어휘.t: 어휘 is the whole vocabulary; a single word is 단어.

불만.x: Customers have a lot of complaints about the service.
불만.t: 불만 is the feeling; to voice it, say 불만을 말하다 or 불평하다.

최선.x: Regardless of the result, I did my best.
최선.t: Set phrase: 최선을 다하다 'to do one's best' — you'll hear 최선을 다하겠습니다 in many speeches.

출신.x: I'm from Busan, so I love the ocean.
출신.e: Literally the place your body 'came out' from.
출신.t: Pattern: [place or school] 출신이에요 means 'I'm from…' or 'I'm a graduate of…'.

전시하다.ex: 이 미술관에서는 현대 미술 작품을 전시하고 있어요.
전시하다.x: This art museum is exhibiting works of modern art.

범인.x: The police caught the culprit in three days.
범인.e: Literally 'a person who committed a crime.'

재산.ex: 그 할아버지는 모든 재산을 학교에 기부했어요.
재산.x: That old man donated his entire fortune to a school.

연애하다.m: to date, to be in a romantic relationship
연애하다.x: The two of them dated for three years and then got married.
연애하다.t: 사귀다 names a partner (민수랑 사귀어요); 연애하다 describes being in a relationship in general.

요인.x: Stress is a major factor that harms your health.

선임.x: I asked a senior colleague about things I didn't know.
선임.e: Literally 'appointed first' — someone who started before you.
선임.t: A different 선임 means 'appointment', as in 대표를 선임하다 (to appoint a CEO).

프로듀서.ex: 그 프로듀서는 인기 예능 프로그램을 많이 만들었어요.
프로듀서.x: That producer has made many popular variety shows.
프로듀서.t: For TV producers Koreans almost always say PD [피디].

성적표.x: I got my report card and showed it to my parents.

체포하다.x: The police arrested the thief right at the scene.
체포하다.t: The passive is 체포되다: 범인이 체포됐어요 'The criminal was arrested.'

벌점.x: I got 15 penalty points for running a red light.
벌점.t: Pronounced [벌쩜]; used for driver's licenses and also for school demerits.

설마.m: surely not, no way, it can't be
설마.x: Surely he didn't lie, did he?
설마.t: Proverb 설마가 사람 잡는다: 'Saying "no way" gets people killed' — don't be careless.

몰아내다.x: The soldiers finally drove the enemy out of the village.

남녀노소.m: people of all ages and genders, everyone
남녀노소.ex: 이 영화는 남녀노소 누구나 즐길 수 있어요.
남녀노소.x: Anyone, young or old, can enjoy this movie.
남녀노소.t: Notice 녀, not 여, because it isn't word-initial; 노 keeps its word-initial form because 노소 'old and young' counts as its own word.

눈코 뜰 새 없다.forms: 눈코 뜰 새 없어요 · 눈코 뜰 새 없었어요 · 눈코 뜰 새 없이 바쁘다
눈코 뜰 새 없다.m: to be extremely busy, to have no time to breathe
눈코 뜰 새 없다.ex: 이번 주는 일이 많아서 눈코 뜰 새 없이 바빴어요.
눈코 뜰 새 없다.x: I had so much work this week that I was crazy busy.
눈코 뜰 새 없다.e: Literally 'no time to even open your eyes and nose'.
nb: 발 없는 말이 천 리 간다

전통 시장.ex: 명절 전에는 전통 시장이 사람들로 붐벼요.
전통 시장.x: Before the holidays, traditional markets are packed with people.

투기.ex: 정부는 부동산 투기를 막기 위해 세금을 올렸어요.
투기.x: The government raised taxes to stop real estate speculation.
투기.t: 투기 sounds negative, like gambling; 투자 (investment) is the neutral word.

내수.x: Exports have increased, but domestic demand is still sluggish.

논지.m: main argument, thesis, point (of an argument)
논지.ex: 글쓴이의 논지가 분명하지 않아서 이해하기 어려워요.
논지.x: The writer's main argument isn't clear, so it's hard to understand.
논지.t: 논지 = what the argument says; 논조 = how it says it (its tone).

고찰하다.m: to examine, to consider, to study (carefully)
고찰하다.ex: 이 논문은 현대 사회의 문제를 깊이 고찰합니다.
고찰하다.x: This paper examines the problems of modern society in depth.

도출하다.m: to derive, to draw (a conclusion), to reach (an agreement)
도출하다.ex: 오랜 논의 끝에 양측은 합의안을 도출했습니다.
도출하다.x: After long discussions, both sides reached a draft agreement.
도출하다.e: Literally 'lead out' — drawing a result out of data or talks.
도출하다.t: Typical objects: 결론·결과·합의·해결책을 도출하다; it's formal, so in speech use 끌어내다.

소각장.ex: 주민들이 새 소각장 건설에 반대하고 있어요.
소각장.x: Residents are opposing the construction of a new incinerator.
소각장.e: 소각 'burning away' + -장 'place', as in 운동장, 주차장.

내포하다.m: to contain, to imply, to connote
내포하다.ex: 이 계획은 여러 가지 문제를 내포하고 있습니다.
내포하다.x: This plan contains a number of problems.
내포하다.e: Literally 'wrapping inside' — holding something hidden within.

구현하다.m: to realize, to embody, to implement
구현하다.ex: 이 건물은 친환경 디자인을 잘 구현했습니다.
구현하다.x: This building realizes eco-friendly design well.
구현하다.e: Literally 'making it appear in concrete form'.

폐지되다.m: to be abolished, to be repealed
폐지되다.x: The system was officially abolished last year.
폐지되다.t: Pronounced [페지되다] — ㅖ after a consonant is usually said like ㅔ.

불러일으키다.m: to arouse, to evoke, to stir up, to cause
불러일으키다.ex: 그 노래는 어린 시절의 추억을 불러일으켜요.
불러일으키다.x: That song brings back childhood memories.
불러일으키다.e: 부르다 'to call' + 일으키다 'to raise up': calling up a feeling.

겸허하다.ex: 그는 팀원들의 비판을 겸허하게 받아들이고 사과했습니다.
겸허하다.x: He humbly accepted his team members' criticism and apologized.
겸허하다.e: Literally 'modest and empty' — keeping no pride inside.
겸허하다.t: Common set phrase: 겸허히 받아들이다 'to humbly accept' (results, criticism), often heard in public apologies.

비단.forms: 비단 A만의 문제가 아니다 — 'not just A's problem'
비단.ex: 환경 문제는 비단 한 나라만의 문제가 아니에요.
비단.x: Environmental problems are not just one country's problem.
비단.t: Almost always followed by -만 … 아니다; don't confuse it with the noun 비단 'silk'.

천재일우.ex: 이런 천재일우의 기회를 놓치면 안 돼요.
천재일우.x: You can't miss a once-in-a-lifetime chance like this.
천재일우.e: Literally 'a meeting that comes once in a thousand years'.
천재일우.t: Don't confuse it with 천재 'genius'; here 재 means 'year'.

이치.m: reason, logic, the natural order of things
이치.ex: 노력한 만큼 얻는 것이 세상의 이치예요.
이치.x: You get as much as you put in; that's how the world works.
이치.e: Literally 'reason reached' — what makes sense by principle.
이치.t: 이치에 맞다 'to make sense' and 이치에 어긋나다 'to be unreasonable' are the key collocations.

수순.ex: 두 회사의 합병은 이제 정해진 수순으로 보여요.
수순.x: The merger of the two companies now looks like a foregone conclusion.
수순.e: Literally 'order of moves'; probably from board games like baduk, where 수 means a move.
수순.t: Common collocations: 수순을 밟다 (go through the steps) and 정해진 수순 (an inevitable course).

근현대사.x: Korea's modern and contemporary history has many painful chapters.
근현대사.e: Blend of 근대 'modern era' and 현대 'contemporary era' + -사 'history'.

서론.ex: 서론에서 연구의 목적을 간단히 밝혀야 해요.
서론.x: You should briefly state the purpose of the study in the introduction.
서론.t: Essays follow 서론 · 본론 · 결론: introduction, body, conclusion.

정확도.ex: 새 프로그램은 번역의 정확도가 훨씬 높아요.
정확도.x: The new program has much higher translation accuracy.

신도.x: Many believers gathered at the church on Easter.

번뇌.m: worldly anguish, earthly desires and suffering
번뇌.x: The monk told us to let go of the anguish in our hearts.
번뇌.e: A Buddhist term: the mental passions that cause suffering.
번뇌.t: Buddhism counts 108 번뇌, which is why prayer beads have 108 beads and people do 108 bows (108배).

전신마취.x: This surgery is done under general anesthesia.
전신마취.t: Say 전신마취를 하다 or 전신마취 상태에서; you 'wake up' from it with 마취에서 깨다.

미주.ex: 이 책은 각주 대신 미주를 사용했어요.
미주.x: This book used endnotes instead of footnotes.
미주.e: Literally 'tail note' — notes at the end of the text.
미주.t: Homonym warning: 미주 (美洲) also means 'the Americas', as in 미주 지역.

기화.x: When water boils, vaporization happens quickly.

입체적 인물.ex: 이 소설의 주인공은 성격이 변하는 입체적 인물이에요.
입체적 인물.x: The main character of this novel is a round character whose personality changes.
입체적 인물.e: Literally 'three-dimensional person' — a character who grows or changes.
입체적 인물.t: 입체적 alone means 'three-dimensional' in everyday use, e.g. 입체적인 그림.

그네뛰기.m: swinging (traditional swing contest, especially on Dano)
그네뛰기.x: When Dano came, women enjoyed swinging contests.
그네뛰기.e: 그네 (swing) + 뛰기 (jumping): you 'jump' a swing in Korean, 그네를 뛰다.
그네뛰기.t: Today, for playground swings, people say 그네를 타다.

난공불락.x: That castle was famous as an impregnable fortress.
난공불락.t: Pronounced [난공불락]; also used for unbeatable champions or tough markets: 난공불락의 시장.

괄시하다.m: to look down on, to treat with contempt, to slight
괄시하다.x: You shouldn't look down on people just because they're poor.
괄시하다.e: Literally 'look at someone indifferently' — treating them as unimportant.
괄시하다.t: Pronounced [괄씨] — tensing after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

범람하다.m: to overflow, to flood; to be flooded with (a glut of something)
범람하다.x: The river overflowed because of the heavy rain.
범람하다.e: Both syllables carry the water radical — water spreading everywhere.
범람하다.t: Pronounced [범남하다] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ.

무구하다.ex: 아이들의 무구한 눈빛을 보면 마음이 맑아져요.
무구하다.x: Seeing the innocent eyes of children makes my heart feel clear.

원대하다.ex: 그는 세계적인 기업을 만들겠다는 원대한 꿈을 품었어요.
원대하다.x: He cherished the grand dream of building a world-class company.

조신하다.ex: 그 아이는 어른들 앞에서 늘 조신하게 행동해요.
조신하다.x: That child always behaves politely in front of adults.
조신하다.e: Literally 'controlling one's body': careful in conduct and manners.

누차.ex: 선생님은 안전 수칙을 지키라고 누차 강조하셨어요.
누차.x: The teacher repeatedly stressed that we follow the safety rules.

문화사대주의.m: cultural toadyism, blind worship of foreign culture
문화사대주의.ex: 외국 것이라면 무조건 좋다고 보는 것은 문화사대주의입니다.
문화사대주의.x: Seeing anything foreign as automatically better is cultural toadyism.
문화사대주의.e: 사대 means 'serving the great', from Joseon's tributary relationship with China.
문화사대주의.t: The mirror image of 자문화중심주의: one overvalues foreign culture, the other one's own.

오염물질.x: Pollutants released from the factory flowed into the river.
오염물질.t: Pronounced [오염물찔]: 질 becomes tense after ㄹ.

교란하다.m: to disturb, to disrupt, to throw into confusion
교란하다.ex: 적의 통신망을 교란하는 것이 작전의 목표였습니다.
교란하다.x: The goal of the operation was to disrupt the enemy's communication network.

현시하다.m: to display, to make manifest, to show clearly
현시하다.ex: 그 기념비는 국가의 권위를 현시하기 위해 세워졌습니다.
현시하다.x: That monument was erected to display the nation's authority.
현시하다.e: Literally 'make manifest and show' — putting something on clear display.

어여쁘다.ex: 할머니는 손녀를 보며 참 어여쁘다고 하셨어요.
어여쁘다.x: Looking at her granddaughter, Grandma said how lovely she was.
어여쁘다.e: An older, poetic form of 예쁘다 'pretty'.
